subject: NorthBay: sudden inference latency and 5xx spike — immediate triage
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@northbay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: NorthBay Ops <ops@northbay.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency spike + 502s across Redwood inference endpoints

Mina / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in p50/p95 latency for the Redwood inference calls powering our checkout personalization (region: us-west-2). Over the last hour requests are intermittently returning 502/504 and p95 latency has jumped from ~120ms to ~1.4s. This started around 07:05 PDT and is impacting ~12% of user traffic.

Attached are a few request traces and a short extract from our synthetic checks: northbay_error_samples.log

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side? We haven't changed anything on our end. This is causing a measurable checkout abandonment lift; we need immediate help.

Happy to hop on a call — available now.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Carter
Head of Infrastructure, NorthBay Retail
emily.carter@northbay.com
+1 415 555 0193

Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + 502s across Redwood inference endpoints

Thanks Emily — we see your alerts. I'm escalating to our network and ops leads and standing up a triage channel.

Immediate asks for your team:
- Can you upload the full pcap for a 1-minute window around 07:05 PDT (filename: packet_capture_northbay_100227.pcap)?
- Share any recent config changes on your VPC peering or peering ACLs.

We're spinning up an initial incident room and will update within 30 min. CC'ing Jonas (network), Vanessa (customer ops), and Rishi (SRE).

—Mina

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Emily Carter <emily.carter@northbay.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 11:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + 502s across Redwood inference endpoints

Emily / team — initial network triage notes below.

What we've observed so far (quick summary):
- Around 07:03 PDT our edge logs show a burst of TCP retransmits and a series of DNS timeouts for northbay-service.us-west-2.redwood.net.
- VPC peering metric stream for the customer's peering connection shows brief route withdrawals (BGP flap-like behavior) between 07:02 and 07:09.
- The majority of 502s appear to correlate with failed backend handoffs where the proxy returned 502 while waiting for an upstream response.

Evidence excerpt (logs):
[07:05:21 PDT] proxy-01 us-west-2 - upstream handshake timeout -> 502
[07:05:31 PDT] resolver-3 us-west-2 - query timeout for northbay-service -> SERVFAIL

Hypothesis: A transient network path instability on the peering path (either at the cloud provider fabric or the customer's edge) caused DNS timeouts and proxy upstream handshakes to fail, producing 502/504s. CloudNet has a maintenance window logged at 07:00 for a subset of routers in us-west-2 — reaching out to them for correlation.

Short-term mitigation options:
1) Force route traffic for NorthBay to the secondary egress (cross-region fallback) while we validate peering stability.
2) Temporarily increase proxy upstream timeouts and enable aggressive retry for idempotent paths (risk: higher client-side latency but fewer 502s).
3) Roll back to last-known-good proxy image for NorthBay (if the issue is proxy binary related).

I'm collecting packet capture; please upload the PCAP Emily referenced. I'll also open a ticket with CloudNet.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Emily Carter <emily.carter@northbay.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 07:45:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + 502s across Redwood inference endpoints

Team — proposed immediate action (minimal blast radius):
- Plan A (preferred): Canary rollback to proxy-image v1.18.2 for NorthBay only (10% -> 50% -> 100% in 20-min increments). This addresses potential proxy-level regressions and is reversible. Rollout plan attached: rollout_plan_northbay.md
- Plan B (if rollback not desirable): Route NorthBay traffic via our secondary egress in us-west-1 (cross-region) and enable prefix-key KV cache bypass for the affected prefix (reduces dependency on upstream DNS resolution during the window).
- Communication: We'll provide customer-facing timeline + SLO impact matrix (slo_impact_northbay.xlsx).

We need a single approver for the rollback and signoff to modify routing. Mina — please confirm and I will start the canary. Also logging/observability will push a dedicated dashboard for this rollout.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Carter <emily.carter@northbay.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 12:30:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + 502s across Redwood inference endpoints

Agree with Vanessa — canary rollback is the fastest, lowest-risk remediation. Operational notes:
- I'll pre-stage the v1.18.2 image in the customer's Dedicated pool and coordinate a rolling restart to keep token-serving capacity intact.
- If we see persistent BGP/peering flaps during the canary, we should immediately failover to cross-region egress.
- I've prepared the emergency commands (netctl route set --customer northbay --egress us-west-1 --force) and will be on the CLI for the canary window.

Also: open a high-priority ticket with CloudNet (I've attached the packet capture they requested).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@northbay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: NorthBay Ops <ops@northbay.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:18:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + 502s across Redwood inference endpoints

Team — quick update from our side: after the canary rollback (v1.18.2) and the temporary cross-region routing, errors dropped to <1% and p95 returned to baseline within ~45 minutes. Thank you for the rapid response.

Two asks from our executive team:
1) A one-page exec summary that explains root cause, mitigation steps, and timelines for full remediation.
2) A postmortem (timeline + action items) and confirmation of whether there will be any SLA credits given the outage length and impact.

We're available for a 30-min sync anytime today.

—Emily

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@northbay.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike + 502s across Redwood inference endpoints

Emily / team — closing notes and next steps:

Status: Service normalized after canary rollback + cross-region fallback. CloudNet has confirmed a routing control-plane maintenance that overlapped with a subset of fabric routers in us-west-2 — they listed it as an unannounced hotfix. We're continuing to push for exact root-cause evidence from CloudNet (ticket: NET-9134).

Deliverables (owner / ETA):
- Exec one-pager (Mina) — draft by 2027-10-05 10:00 PDT -> shared to drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident-reports/NORTHBAY-2027-10
- Technical postmortem with packet captures and BGP logs (Jonas) — 2027-10-07 EOD
- SLA credit evaluation + support case (Vanessa + Billing) — 2027-10-06
- Implementation of improved egress routing safeguards (Rishi) — design by 2027-10-10

Thanks for your patience and the rapid collaboration. We'll get the formal docs to you and set a short exec sync after the one-pager is ready.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
